samples.summary: `saveSnapshot()` before `withUndoUnit()` double-counts undo on MemDocStore, so every batched edit costs a dead Cmd+Z in slides text boxes and the docs demo app
samples.evidence: The new rule is "`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one" (text-editor.ts:3807, docs-collaboration.md:335). On `MemDocStore` the undo unit is anchored to the checkpoint, not to an update: `snapshot()` pushes a clone (memory.ts:177-184) and then `batch()` pushes *another* pre-body clone up front (memory.ts:199-209), skipping the double-push only when `batchDepth > 0`. So `handleInput`/`handleEnter`/`applyPastePlan`/`pasteFromClipboard` now push two identical undo entries per action: the first Cmd+Z restores the pre-edit document, the second appears to do nothing and consumes a history slot. This is exactly the "first Cmd+Z looked like it did nothing" symptom `withNamedStyleChange` avoids by calling `docStore.snapshot()` *inside* `doc.batch()` (editor.ts:1238-1239). MemDocStore is not dev-only: slides text boxes run this same `TextEditor` with `MemDocStore` and wire `saveSnapshot = () => docStore.snapshot()` and `undoAction = () => docStore.undo()` (text-box-editor.ts:431, 680-683), so Slides in-textbox undo is affected in production. Nothing in the diff (contract text in store.ts, memory.ts, or the new tests, which all use `YorkieDocStore`) covers the Mem path.

samples.summary: The undo-floor-as-identity fix lands only in YorkieDocStore; the three sibling stores keep the depth pattern and still cite the removed `undoFloor` as their reference
samples.evidence: `yorkie-slides-store.ts:347/358/654/670`, `yorkie-note-store.ts:127/136/353` and `yorkie-board-store.ts:244/270/514` all compare `getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor` — the comparison this diff proves stops describing the boundary once the 50-entry cap drops entries — and their comments say "Mirrors `YorkieDocStore.undoFloor`", a field that no longer exists after this change. `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:183-209` still prescribes the depth version as the reference implementation and names `docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` as the reference impl (line 323). The repo now has two answers to "where is the undo floor", and the canonical doc documents the wrong one. The issue's Non-goals do not cover this either way (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:49-54).

samples.summary: Paste undo-cost test docstring still asserts the opposite of the new `applyPastePlan` contract
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites `applyPastePlan`'s doc comment to "One undo unit … `withUndoUnit` folds all of them into a single `doc.update()`" and points at this test file as the pin, but the test's own header (lines 132-147) was left saying "Batching the middle blocks collapses that to a constant, but *not* to one: `insertBlocks()` still … as separate store writes", and the assertion comment at line 215 still reads "Measured at 4". A reader is now given two contradictory statements about the same behavior in the two places the change explicitly cross-references.

samples.summary: Other per-block-write actions over a large selection are still one undo unit per block, so the issue's stated Goal ("the 50-entry cap is never reached by a single keystroke") is only met for selection-replacing edits
samples.evidence: The todo's Goal is "One user action = one undo unit for every selection-replacing edit, so the 50-entry cap is never reached by a single keystroke" (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-todo.md:22-25), and its lessons file says auditing the per-block call sites is "the other half" of the work. `handleTab` still writes one `setBlockType` per selected list item (text-editor.ts:2739-2750), as do the block-style / block-type sweeps at text-editor.ts:2784, 2805 and editor.ts:3351, 3512, 3534, 3557 — none is wrapped in `withUndoUnit`/`doc.batch`. Tab over a 100-item select-all therefore still pushes ~100 units and evicts 50 real entries of history. No content is destroyed by these paths (unlike the delete), so the cost is a truncated history rather than lost text, hence minor; but it leaves the stated goal partially unmet.
searchedFor: grep `deleteSelection\(\)` in packages/docs/src (all 17 call sites reviewed)

samples.summary: The render hold is implemented by shadowing one field, so the other render entry points bypass the documented "paint stays outside the batch" rule
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit` holds paint by wrapping only the private `requestRender` field (text-editor.ts:711-723). The two sibling render variants `requestRenderNoCursorScroll` (line 232) and `requestCursorRender` (line 244) are public, host-assigned and call the host directly, so any future write path that repaints through them inside a unit paints mid-batch — the rule the doc states as invariant is enforced for one of three entry points rather than at a single seam.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. text-editor.ts:3807 does state the "saveSnapshot() before the unit, never inside" rule, and handleInput (995-1001), insertText (814-816) and applyPastePlan (1532-1533) follow it. On MemDocStore that sequence double-pushes: snapshot() pushes a clone unconditionally outside a batch (memory.ts:177-184) and batch() then pushes its own pre-body clone (memory.ts:206-209), whose wroteNothing pop (memory.ts:230-236) cannot fire because the body did write. undo() (memory.ts:157-161) does no dedup, so the second Cmd+Z restores an identical document and burns a history slot. Reachable in production, not just dev: text-box-editor.ts:431 instantiates MemDocStore and wires saveSnapshot (line 680) and undoAction (681-687) into the same TextEditor, and packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts consumes initializeTextBox; Cmd+Z reaches undoAction at text-editor.ts:1273-1280. The correct pattern exists a few files over — withNamedStyleChange calls docStore.snapshot() inside doc.batch (editor.ts:1238-1239), where Mem's batchDepth>0 early return makes it free. docs-collaboration.md:335-336 claims "On MemDocStore it is just a checkpoint," which memory.ts:199-209 contradicts, and memory.test.ts covers snapshot-inside-batch (238-268) and unbatched snapshots (271) but never snapshot-then-batch. Two implementations of one documented seam now give two different answers to "how many undo units is one user action," with a user-visible cost on the Slides surface, so it is major and in this lens's lane rather than a line-level correctness nit. No guard, no dedup, no caller-side interception found.
